ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=2$, $AD=4$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, $F$ is a moving point on the line segment $EC$, $P$ is the midpoint of $BF$. When the line segment $PD$ is drawn, what is the range of possible values for $PD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram:\\
When point F coincides with point C, point P is at ${P}_{1}$, where $C{P}_{1}=B{P}_{1}$,\\
When point F coincides with point E, point P is at ${P}_{2}$, where $E{P}_{2}=B{P}_{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}\parallel EC$ and ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}CE$,\\
When point F lies on EC excluding points C and E, we have BP=FP,\\
By the Midline Theorem, it is known that: ${P}_{1}P\parallel CF$ and ${P}_{1}P=\frac{1}{2}CF$,\\
$\therefore$ The trajectory of point P is the line segment ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}$,\\
$\because$ In rectangle ABCD, AB=2, AD=4, E is the midpoint of AD,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABE$, $\triangle BEC$, $\triangle DCP_{1}$ are isosceles right triangles,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ECB=45^\circ$, $\angle DP_{1}C=45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}\parallel EC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle P_{2}P_{1}B=\angle ECB=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle P_{2}P_{1}D=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ The length of DP is smallest at $D{P}_{1}$ and largest at $D{P}_{2}$,\\
$\because$ $CD=C{P}_{1}=DE=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $D{P}_{1}=2\sqrt{2}$, $CE=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}=\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $D{P}_{2}=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{2})^2}=\sqrt{10}$,\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{2\sqrt{2}\le PD\le \sqrt{10}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=2$, $AD=4$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, $F$ is a moving point on the line segment $EC$, $P$ is the midpoint of $BF$. When the line segment $PD$ is drawn, what is the range of possible values for $PD$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram:\\
When point F coincides with point C, point P is at ${P}_{1}$, where $C{P}_{1}=B{P}_{1}$,\\
When point F coincides with point E, point P is at ${P}_{2}$, where $E{P}_{2}=B{P}_{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}\parallel EC$ and ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}CE$,\\
When point F lies on EC excluding points C and E, we have BP=FP,\\
By the Midline Theorem, it is known that: ${P}_{1}P\parallel CF$ and ${P}_{1}P=\frac{1}{2}CF$,\\
$\therefore$ The trajectory of point P is the line segment ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}$,\\
$\because$ In rectangle ABCD, AB=2, AD=4, E is the midpoint of AD,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABE$, $\triangle BEC$, $\triangle DCP_{1}$ are isosceles right triangles,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ECB=45^\circ$, $\angle DP_{1}C=45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}\parallel EC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle P_{2}P_{1}B=\angle ECB=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle P_{2}P_{1}D=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ The length of DP is smallest at $D{P}_{1}$ and largest at $D{P}_{2}$,\\
$\because$ $CD=C{P}_{1}=DE=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $D{P}_{1}=2\sqrt{2}$, $CE=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ ${P}_{1}{P}_{2}=\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $D{P}_{2}=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{2})^2}=\sqrt{10}$,\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{2\sqrt{2}\le PD\le \sqrt{10}}$

F moves on EC, so one may set F=(2+2t,2-2t), where 0≤t≤1; when t=0, F=E, and when t=1, F=C. Because P is the midpoint of BF, P=((2+2t)/2,(2-2t)/2)=(1+t,1-t).
